residents.name: Gurupriyan
residents.notes: no curd in any form; dislikes raw onion (cooked fine, deep-fried/burnt onions loved); coriander tastes like soap on some days; dislikes shellfish; borderline mutton aversion; paneer max once per 2 weeks; no tomato in raita

residents.name: Raksha
residents.notes: loves shellfish; dislikes methi (fenugreek); dislikes golden-fried/deep-fried food (except fried onions in biryani); dislikes restaurant-style tomato; dislikes eating carried-over fridge food

pets.portioning_note: Portioning for humans only; cat not fed from the plan.

cook.name: Yasmeen Didi
cook.schedule: Mon-Sat, 7:00-7:30 AM arrival, one visit/day; all three meals prepped in the morning, dinner cooked in the afternoon and held
notes: Recipe videos must have on-screen text or spoken narration with exact ingredients and quantities; not too fast-paced.
Fish prep is a skill gap - household wants more fish; coach rather than avoid.
Photographs fruits/veg/eggs/milk/bread/paneer/curd/meat daily post-cooking, each as a separate photo.

person_rules.note: Gurupriyan does not eat curd in any form - any curd-based dish or side is for Raksha's portion only. Never a shared curd main.
Shellfish disliked by Gurupriyan (Raksha loves them) - do not default to shellfish for shared meals; per-person call.
Bhindi only acceptable 'bhagwan bhindi' style (style undefined - confirm before serving). Excluded until confirmed.
Onions must be fully cooked or deep-fried/burnt, never raw-served (e.g. no raw onion salad/kachumber).
Use sparingly / on the side rather than mixed in.
Methi disliked by Raksha - avoid in her portion; prefer dishes without methi as a hero.
Golden-fried / deep-fried food disliked (exception: fried onions in biryani). Prefer roasted, grilled, air-fried.

slot_ingredient_bans.note: Hard stop: no rice, no cucumber at dinner/night, across all days.

dish_keyword_rules.note: Sandwiches go soggy by night - breakfast/lunch only.
Raita: onion + carrot base, never tomato + curd.
Rice-based dishes are not served at night.

frequency_caps.name: Chicken as hero
frequency_caps.note: Chicken 1-2x/week as the hero (no separate veg dish needed that meal); boneless preferred; buy fresh on the day.

frequency_caps.name: Paneer
frequency_caps.note: Paneer not more than once every 2 weeks (Gurupriyan).

frequency_caps.name: Fish
frequency_caps.note: Household wants more fish; cook needs coaching - include a video link.

ingredient_grade_rules.rule: Ponni white rice for daily use; basmati only for Hyderabadi dishes; jeera rice for biryani/ghee rice; red rice NOT preferred - do not substitute.
Boneless cut preferred over curry-cut/bone-in; buy fresh/frozen on the day of cooking.
Home-quality tomatoes; Raksha dislikes restaurant-style tomato taste - sensory check at sourcing.
'Lentils' in this household means masoor dal.

breakfast_style: Karnataka/Kerala leaning (neer dosa, idli + stew, upma, pathiri) is the preferred register; egg/veg sandwiches and whole grains (wheat/rye/soba/rava) encouraged.

cooking_technique.oil_salt: Sparing but justified - not zero-oil, not excess
cooking_technique.equipment: Air fryer actively used for lower-oil cooking; use for anything that would otherwise be deep-fried
cooking_technique.onions: Always cooked through or deep-fried/burnt; never raw-served
cooking_technique.coriander: Under-season; offer fresh garnish on the side
cooking_technique.batching: Cook a large batch at lunch (e.g. chana masala, butter chicken) and carry to dinner with rotis - normal practice

nutrition_direction: Higher protein + greens, reduced oil (wedding prep)
Gradual introduction of salads (no cucumber), egg/veg sandwiches, whole grains
More fish in rotation for lean protein variety
weekend_pattern: Saturday/Sunday skew toward pasta or biryani (cooked by Gurupriyan himself); Sunday is the cook's day off.
standing_instructions: Curd: Gurupriyan does not eat curd - restrict to Raksha's portion only.
Night meals: avoid rice and cucumber at dinner, across all days.
Sandwiches are not for dinner (go soggy).
Salads: no cucumber; corn goes into a mixed salad rather than a separate corn salad.
Dry veg + curry carried to dinner with rotis is the standard approach.
Don't repeat a heavily-used ingredient/dish from the prior week (e.g. drumstick twice).
Carrot in the moong dal breakfast made it too sweet - avoid carrot in that dish specifically.
Portions strictly for 2 residents - no planned leftovers; nothing kept beyond 1 day (chapati only if the side is mild).
Cut fruit + snack veggies (carrot, cucumber, sweetcorn) kept visibly on the table daily.
Check pantry stock (green chilli, coconut, drumsticks, sambar onions) before adding to cart - avoid duplicate ordering.
No proactive disposal of purchased vegetables - plan meals to use everything bought.
Place ingredient orders the evening/night before, not the morning of.
Lunchbox: pack Gurupriyan's lunchbox the same way breakfast is handled.
Meal plan for next day sent the evening before via WhatsApp, with a YouTube link for unfamiliar dishes; instructions in simple Hindi.
non_negotiables: No rice or cucumber at night.
Curry leaves, green chilli, coriander always in stock - never let these run out.
Raita: onion + carrot base, never tomato + curd.
notes: 'Bhagwan bhindi' style is undefined - confirm before serving bhindi (excluded until then).
Dinner being afternoon-cooked and held till evening is the house norm, not a freshness issue.
Guests: notify ops proactively; ~Rs100/guest/day; adjust plan for longer stays.
